skill.name: image-to-video
skill.description: Route image-to-video requests to RunComfy models for still-image animation, custom voiceover lip-sync, and multi-modal reference workflows.
skill.summary: Choose a RunComfy image-to-video route and draft model-specific prompts.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and example field names. Confirmed risks remain for intentional external CLI execution, token persistence, third-party media processing, and an installation-source mismatch.

remediation.issue: Installation instructions point to a different repository owner.
remediation.suggestion: Align the GitHub link and npx install command with the audited repository, or document signed provenance for the alternate source.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on global npm and RunComfy CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before installation or execution, pin package versions, and document the exact CLI package source.

remediation.issue: RunComfy login stores an API token in a hidden config file.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer short-lived tokens for automation, document token revocation, and keep file permissions restricted to the owner.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media references are sent to third-party RunComfy services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear consent warning and advise users not to submit confidential media, private voice recordings, or regulated data.

content.value_statement: Choosing the right image-to-video model can waste credits and time. This skill routes each request to a RunComfy model and supplies model-specific prompts.
actual_capabilities: Routes still-image animation requests across HappyHorse 1.0, Wan 2.7, and Seedance 2.0 Pro.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for each supported model route.
Recommends HappyHorse for portraits, products, and general image-to-video animation.
Recommends Wan 2.7 when a custom voiceover URL should drive lip-sync.
Recommends Seedance for workflows with image, video, and audio references.
Lists model inputs, limits, exit codes, and security notes for RunComfy use.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account, local CLI setup, and valid authentication.
Uses external media URLs that RunComfy services may fetch and process.
Clip duration, resolution, and aspect behavior depend on the selected model.
Does not combine multiple model routes into one generated clip.

use_cases.title: Create Product Motion Clips
use_cases.description: Turn product stills into short reveal, orbit, or macro-motion clips with model-specific prompt guidance.

use_cases.title: Generate Voiceover Variants
use_cases.description: Route portrait or spokesperson requests to a lip-sync workflow when a custom audio URL is available.

use_cases.title: Blend Reference Media
use_cases.description: Use subject images, scene videos, and audio references to plan multi-modal RunComfy generation requests.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Still Animation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for simple motion from one image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this image URL: [image URL]. Use gentle motion, keep the subject stable, and save the result to [output folder].

prompt_templates.title: Product Reveal Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for controlled product movement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short product reveal from [image URL]. Use a slow orbit, stable packaging text, clean lighting, and a five-second duration.

prompt_templates.title: Custom Voiceover Lip-Sync
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with a portrait image and audio URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate a spokesperson using [portrait image URL] and lip-sync to [audio URL]. Match the clip length to the audio and avoid subtitles.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Modal Reference Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using image, video, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [subject image], [scene video], and [voice audio] to create one clip. Preserve subject identity and follow the reference scene mood.

output_examples.input: A portrait photo needs subtle movement while preserving identity.
output_examples.output: The skill selects HappyHorse 1.0 I2V, recommends a short 1080P clip, and drafts a motion-focused prompt.

output_examples.input: A headshot and voiceover URL are provided for a vertical ad.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Wan 2.7 with custom audio, matches duration to the voiceover, and suggests useful negative prompts.

output_examples.input: A subject image, cafe video, and voice reference should guide one clip.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Seedance 2.0 Pro and maps the references to subject, scene, and voice cues.

best_practices: Use one main motion beat per clip so the model has a clear visual goal.
Keep identity, branding, and geometry preservation goals explicit in the prompt.
Confirm consent before sending private images, voice recordings, or brand assets to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential media URLs without reviewing RunComfy handling requirements.
Do not mix unrelated visual styles across reference images and videos.
Do not request one clip that requires several model routes at once.

faq.question: Which model does the skill use by default?
faq.answer: It defaults to HappyHorse 1.0 I2V for general still-image animation requests.

faq.question: Can it use a custom voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes custom voiceover lip-sync requests to the Wan 2.7 workflow with an audio URL.

faq.question: Can it combine image, video, and audio references?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Seedance 2.0 Pro guidance for multi-modal reference workflows.

faq.question: Does it generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to submit jobs to RunComfy remote services.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Users need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, authentication, and valid source media URLs.

faq.question: What privacy concern should users review?
faq.answer: Prompts and media references may be processed by RunComfy services, so sensitive assets need extra review.
